key_insight: Embed Pauli propagation inside a noise-canceling hybrid workflow so a classically modified observable can be measured on hardware with less sampling overhead and lower truncation error.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to more accurate observable estimation on noisy quantum processors by balancing quantum measurements with classical post-processing.
method: Propagate the target observable through inverse noise channels to form a noise-canceled observable.
Measure the modified observable directly on the quantum processor instead of the original one.
Use hybrid truncation strategies to control classical memory/runtime while limiting propagation error.
evidence_signal: The authors benchmarked the approach numerically on canonical models and experimentally on a 56-qubit superconducting processor, comparing truncation tradeoffs.
watch_item: Performance depends on the chosen truncation strategy, so gains may be offset if inverse-channel propagation becomes too costly or unstable.
paper_title: Computing noise-canceling observables via Pauli propagation
